audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer credits Lissandra with a shield in nine separate places — 'shielded poke pattern', 'her passive shield absorbs your damage', 'a point-blank Claw self-shield', 'shield economy', 'shield through anything you throw back', 'All-in with her passive shield up'. Lissandra has no shield anywhere in her kit.
audit.why: Her passive is Iceborn Subjugation: enemy champions who die near her become Frozen Thralls that slow and then shatter. Glacial Path is an ice claw plus a teleport to it. Ring of Frost is a 450-range root. Frozen Tomb heals and grants invulnerability only when self-cast on a 120s cooldown. Nothing in the kit absorbs damage. The whole early-game plan on this page is built on an ability she does not have.
audit.corrected: Her early strength is Ice Shard — 725 range, 7s at rank 1 falling to 3s at rank 5 — plus a 450-range Ring of Frost root, not a shield. Play outside 450 and respect the Q cadence.

audit.whatIsWrong: Frozen Tomb's self-cast (untargetable, invulnerable, and a self-heal) is never mentioned, and neither is Crystallize's answer to Glacial Path.
audit.why: Both are flagged in missingInteractions and both are in Riot's text: 'If cast on Lissandra, she encases herself in dark ice, healing herself while becoming untargetable and invulnerable.' Anivia's whole commit is a slow zone plus a stun — every point of it is wasted if it goes into the self-cast. And Glacial Path only teleports her to where the claw actually got to, so terrain across the claw's line caps her escape.
audit.corrected: Wait out the self-cast rather than spending R and Q into it, and buy Oblivion Orb for the heal. Wall the line she throws the claw down — she can only arrive where the claw reached.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0..4].side all read 'Skill' while win[0..4] read Lissandra; and packet.defects flags 'level chart contradicts data: Anivia wins 52.18% but the chart gives Lissandra 5/7 stages vs 2'.
audit.why: Two layers render two answers to the same rows, and the shared answer is itself too generous to Lissandra for a 52.18% Anivia win rate. Level 6 is Anivia's largest spike in the game — Glacial Storm — while Frozen Tomb arrives at 120s at rank 1, the rarest cooldown in the lane. The page's own breakdown.mid already says 'Post-6 the lane inverts'.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 Lissandra (Ice Shard cadence and the 450 root), rows 4-6 Anivia (Glacial Storm, then Seraph's/RoA). phases[0..3].side = Lissandra; phases[4].side = Anivia paired with win[4] = Anivia.

audit.whatIsWrong: Lissandra is referred to as male throughout the full layer, and the difficulty story is built on the non-existent shield.
audit.why: Same fabrication as point 4, plus wrong pronouns.
audit.corrected: Difficulty is a poke-and-root lane pre-6 and a zone lane after: stay outside 450, punish the 24s Glacial Path, and take over at Glacial Storm.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal timing despite Frozen Tomb's self-heal.
audit.corrected: Oblivion Orb before extended fights against a Lissandra who self-casts.

edits.after: - Glacial Path: 24s at rank 1 down to 12s at rank 5 — she is immobile that whole time. - Ring of Frost: 10s and only 450 range, so respect the last step in, not the walk up. - Frozen Tomb: 120s at rank 1, and self-cast it is untargetable plus a heal — wait it out.

edits.before: Lissandra's shielded poke pattern outclasses your early trades — her passive triggers off any hit she takes, absorbing your Flash Frost damage while her Ice Shard chips you down for free, and this holds true from level 1 all the way to 5. You have to play patiently here, avoiding extended trades and using Frostbite mainly for wave clear rather than forcing fights you're likely to lose on raw damage exchange.

She has no shield of any kind; what punishes you is the cadence and the 450-range Ring of Frost. Play patiently: stay outside 450, use Frostbite for wave clear, and save Crystallize for her claw.

notes: The largest defect on this page is a fabricated ability: nine separate strings across the content layer describe a Lissandra shield (passive shield, Claw self-shield, shield economy). She has no shield — her passive is Iceborn Subjugation, which creates Frozen Thralls from champions who die near her. Every affected string is corrected here. Level chart rebuilt as one atomic group to clear the flagged win-rate contradiction: rows 0-3 Lissandra, rows 4-6 Anivia, with the row-4 flip proposed as a matched pair (phases[4].side + win[4]) and rows 0-3 needing only the full half because the content layer already held Lissandra. The row-4 flip is a judgement call — the packet flags the old chart as wrong but does not say where the correct flip sits; Glacial Storm at 6 against a 120s Frozen Tomb is the justification.
